subject: Encryption access models, evidence checklist, and next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@finserve-example.com>, FinServe Security Team <security@finserve-example.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Encryption requirements — notes + asks

Thanks again for taking the call this morning, Priya. Quick recap + concrete asks so we can keep momentum toward the security review: 

Summary of what we heard (high level)
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ required; mTLS preferred for service-to-service connections
- At-rest: AES-256 or equivalent; customer must be able to bring/manage keys (BYOK) for production workloads
- HSM: hardware-backed key custody is preferred for keys that encrypt PII
- Audit/logging: request to surface per-request metadata (request id, model id, token counts) and 12+ month immutable audit retention for key use events
- Residency: production inference must run in your managed VPC / us-east region with strict egress controls

Concrete asks / next steps for FinServe: 
1) Confirm which key custody model you prefer: Redwood-managed CMK (standard), Customer-managed CMK in Redwood cloud KMS, or External HSM via Bring-Your-Own-Key (HSM via AWS CloudHSM / on-prem HSM gateway).
2) Share the specific compliance evidence you need from us for the PoC vs. production (examples: KMS design diagram, key rotation policy, key use audit samples, SOC 2 control pages).
3) Provide a list of the team members who will join a 60-min technical workshop (security + infra) next week; suggested owners: Priya (security), one infra/SRE, and a procurement contact.

What we can provide (by Thursday EOD):
- Lightweight KMS/HSM options doc (design patterns, pros/cons, latency/cost impact) — will attach
- Example key-use audit sample (redacted) and SOC 2 snapshot — will attach
- A short checklist for the technical workshop to speed prep

Attachments sent with this message: redwood_kms_design-2027.pdf (design patterns), soc2-snapshot.pdf (public SOC 2 excerpt)

If you prefer, we can run the workshop as two 30-min blocks: HSM/KMS design and audit/logging & retention. Let me know what timing works.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <pshah@finserve-example.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Encryption requirements — notes + asks

Adding some security detail from our side that I think will matter to the FinServe reviewers: 

1) BYOK models we support (short):
- Redwood-managed KMS (default): we manage keys, rotate quarterly, provide key-use logs. Lowest friction for PoC.
- Customer-managed CMK in cloud KMS (recommended intermediate): customer owns root, we encrypt data keys with the customer CMK. This gives you control over key lifecycle and key deletion.
- External HSM (highest assurance): we support connectivity to customer HSMs (CloudHSM or on-prem HSM via a secure gateway). This requires an HSM connector VM in your VPC and an MFA/ops process for key provisioning.

2) Audit/logging: we can emit signed key-use events to your logging endpoint (syslog/HTTPS) and retain an immutable copy in our audit storage for N months — we can set retention windows by contract. Typical ask: 12–36 months.

3) Proof points: I'll attach a redacted sample of key-use logs and the high-level KMS architecture diagram. For production we can also run a short onboarding session with our ops team to walk through the HSM connector provisioning flow.

Low-risk defaults for PoC: use customer-managed CMK in your cloud KMS (fast to set up) + 12-month audit retention. If we need hardware-backed attestation we can escalate to HSM during production onboarding.

Ben Carter
Director, Security Engineering | Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence-request-template.xlsx

-----Original message-----
From: Priya Shah <pshah@finserve-example.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinServe Security Team <security@finserve-example.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 08:07:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Encryption requirements — notes + asks

Hi Dylan / Ben,

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing internally this morning: 

- For PoC, FinServe prefers customer-managed CMK in our cloud KMS (we are on AWS). We want to validate that Redwood can encrypt model data keys with our CMK and that Redwood metadata does not include raw PII.
- For production, our compliance org will expect HSM-backed keys for keys that encrypt PII. We'll need an architecture diagram showing the HSM connector and where key material resides at each stage.
- Audit retention: 24 months minimum for key-use events and immutable tamper-evidence for that period. Can Redwood provide signed audit files that we can ingest into our SIEM?
- Residency: PoC can run in your hosted environment in us-east, but production will require deployment inside our VPC with no egress except to our approved destinations.

Attached is a short spreadsheet with the evidence items we typically ask vendors to provide. For timeline, procurement/infosec wants the PoC kickoff next Tuesday; can you confirm availability for a 60-min technical workshop Monday or Tuesday morning EST?

Priya Shah
Senior Security Architect, FinServeBank

Attachment referenced: vendor-evidence-ask.xlsx (they will send a formal doc from procurement later)

Dylan / Ben — I can run the workshop and will prepare a short runbook for the HSM connector flow. I recommend we propose two 30-min blocks on Tuesday 5/11 10:00–10:30 EST (KMS options + PoC steps) and 10:45–11:15 EST (HSM connector + audit ingestion).

Scheduling: I will send a calendar invite pending Priya confirmation.

Marissa Cole
